News.title: When does Andy Burnham become PM? Exact date and time he could lead the country – and what the process is
News.content:
WESTMINSTER is gearing up for a transition, as the “King of the North” prepares to claim the Prime Minister’s office.

Following Sir Keir Starmer’s resignation last month, former Greater Manchester Mayor Andy Burnham is on track to Downing Street.

Here is everything you need to know about exactly when Burnham will take charge, whether anyone can stop him, and the bizarre royal protocols he must complete to become Britain’s next Prime Minister.



When will Andy Burnham become PM?

Burnham is expected to officially become Prime Minister on Monday, July 20.



But before he can head to Buckingham Palace, he must first officially take the reins of his party.

He is expected to be formally confirmed as the new Labour leader at a special party conference on Friday, July 17.

On Monday morning, the transition of power will begin, with Keir Starmer holding a final briefing before he departs Downing Street.



Starmer will then travel to Buckingham Palace to formally tender his resignation to King Charles III.

Burnham will also travel to the Palace, where the King will officially invite him to form a new government.

He is likely to officially become Britain’s Prime Minister at around 11.30am, immediately following this formal audience.

Then, Burnham will travel back to Downing Street as Prime Minister, stepping up to the famous black door to deliver his first address to the nation.



Could a surprise challenger upset the race?

The race to become the next Labour leader – and therefore Prime Minister – is mathematically won.

Under Labour party rules, any challenger needs the formal backing of at least 81 MPs to get on the ballot.

Burnham secured 369 nominations out of 403 eligible Labour MPs – that represents over 91% of the Parliamentary Labour Party.

MP Catherine West was nominated but failed to gain traction, securing just 1 nomination.

Because Burnham secured an overwhelming majority of nominations, it is mathematically impossible for any other candidate to reach the 81-MP threshold.



The contest is effectively over, meaning there’s no chance of a last-minute surprise challenger throwing a spanner in the works.

What is the process for Burnham to be sworn in as PM?

Becoming Prime Minister involves a fascinating mix of modern politics and centuries-old royal quirks and traditions.

News.title: Full list of UK train stations rolling out major change to ticket barriers in new £33m crackdown
News.content:
A MAJOR change is coming to ticket barriers across some of Britain’s biggest train stations.

The move comes as part of a £33.4million investment plan issued by the Department for Transport.



New ticket barriers will be introduced to a number of railway stations across England in a crackdown on fare dodging.

Earlier today, The Department for Transport announced that £33.4million in investment would be given to railway operators to fund the rollout.



Barriers featuring taller paddle doors, intended to prevent people from jumping over gates, will be installed in Britain’s “fare dodger hotspots”.

Waist-high barriers, similar to those used on the London Underground network, will also be introduced more frequently as part of the measure.



Industry body, the Railway Delivery Group, suggests at least £350million to £400million a year of fare revenue is lost on fraud and ticketless travel.

In response, rail minister Lord Hendy said: “Fare evasion is not a victimless crime – it undermines confidence in the railway and means passengers lose out on millions in revenue which should be invested to improve services for everyone.”

As a result, six different rail operators will install new barriers across 18 different stations.

Avanti West Coast, East Midlands Railway, Great Anglia, Thameslink Southern Great Northern, TransPennine Express and West Midlands Train will all share the funding throughout stations all around the the UK.



TransPennine Express is set to install barriers at Manchester Piccadilly, one of the busiests railway stations outside of London with over 27 million annual passengers and 14 platforms.

Liverpool Lime Street will further see funding by Avanti West Coast, welcoming over 14 million passengers annually.

Commuter stations Stevenage, Worthing, Elephant and Castle and Stafford are part of the fund too.

Market Harborough, Hertford East, Manningtree, Rayleigh, Ware, Witham, Gipsy Hill, Royston, Nuneaton, Tamowrth, Worcester Foregate Street and Worcester Shrub Hill make up the total 18 stations.

Lord Hendy continued: “By stopping fare dodgers before they reach the platform, we’re protecting taxpayer cash, supporting investment in the network and ensuring the railway works better for the millions of passengers who do the right thing every day by paying their way.”



The rollout of the new gates is expected to begin in early 2027, and set to be completed by mid-2028.

News.title: Will Keir Starmer be going to the World Cup final?
News.content:
THOMAS Tuchel’s Three Lions are just one win away from a historic World Cup final.

Tonight (July 15), England take on Argentina in a blockbuster semi-final clash in Atlanta.

If they march on, they will face Spain in New Jersey on Sunday, July 19. But the biggest drama might not be on the pitch.



Sunday is also outgoing Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer’s last day in office before handing over the keys of Downing Street.



Can the football-mad PM make a dramatic dash to the US, cheer on the lads, and fly home in time to resign?

Will Keir Starmer be going to the World Cup final?

Sir Keir, a die-hard Arsenal season ticket holder, has made no secret of his love for the beautiful game.

Behind the scenes, No10 officials are said to be mapping out a potential high-stakes trip to the New York New Jersey Stadium in East Rutherford if England make it to the final.

The PM has strongly hinted he will cross the Atlantic for the event, in what would be his final international appearance representing Great Britain.

Insiders say Starmer is desperate to see England lift their first World Cup since 1966 in person, and he isn’t going to let a little thing like moving out of Downing Street stop him.

Was the timing deliberate?

Sir Keir announced his resignation on June 22, and the subsequent Labour leadership contest was structured so that his successor – Andy Burnham – will officially take charge on Monday, July 20.

This means Starmer’s final full day as PM lands on Sunday, July 19 – the exact day of the World Cup final. Coincidence? Or tactical diary planning?



While Downing Street insists the timeline was dictated purely by party rules, it is certainly convenient.

How will he get home to hand over power?

The World Cup final kicks off at 8pm UK time (3pm local time in New Jersey) on Sunday.

If the game goes to extra time and penalties, it won’t finish until at least 11pm UK time.

Burnham is scheduled to officially become Prime Minister on Monday morning, July 20, likely around 11.30am.

Before that can happen, Sir Keir must travel to Buckingham Palace to formally tender his resignation to King Charles III. So how will he pull it off?



Starmer will have to board the RAF Voyager private ministerial jet immediately after the final whistle.

The flight from New York to London takes roughly seven hours.

Because the UK is five hours ahead of New York, an overnight flight leaving at 8pm US time (1am Monday UK time) won’t land in London until Monday 8am.

Starmer will have to dash to New Jersey’s Newark Liberty Airport soon after the match, sleep on the plane, head straight from Heathrow to Downing Street for a final briefing, and then on to the Palace.

A transatlantic travel delay on his way back from New Jersey could push back the official handover of power and leave Burnham waiting in the wings.



Could he declare an extra bank holiday?

If football comes home, the nation will want a party, and Starmer has already set the wheels in motion.

Speaking at the NATO summit earlier this month, Sir Keir teased: “On the question of a bank holiday, I don’t want to jinx it, but ask me again if we get to the final.”

Behind closed doors, officials are reportedly drawing up for an extra public holiday.

The proposed date is Friday, July 24, which would allow the England squad time to fly back from the States and let the FA stage a massive victory parade through London.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Technically, because Starmer officially steps down on Monday morning, the final sign-off for the bank holiday would likely fall to Burnham.



But Starmer could announce his intention to grant the holiday on Sunday night as a final act of goodwill, leaving Burnham to rubber-stamp it on his first day on the job.

News.title: Five BBQ items BANNED from household bins – ignoring could land you with a £400 fine
News.content:
WITH the summer weather in full swing, many Brits are venturing outside for a barbecue.

And while there’s nothing better than a tasty al fresco meal in the hot weather, make sure you’re not making these common mistakes when it comes to the clean up.



While its definitely more tempting to have a barbecue in your garden instead of sweating away in a hot kitchen, you can often be left with a lot of rubbish.

And many households are unaware of the correct way to dispose of these items.



In fact, there are five common things you should never place in your bins when cleaning up after a barbecue.

You can even land yourself with a £400 fine if you ignore this guidance.



Aluminium trays

While you may be tempted to place the foil trays used for cooking meat and vegetables into your recycling bin, you need to take an extra step first.

“If trays are heavily contaminated with grease, food residue or burnt material, they may not be suitable for recycling collections.” James Ward, waste expert at Wheeldon Brothers, told the Express.

Make sure to check your local council’s guidance before placing them in your recycling bin.

And if they are allowed in the recycling bins in your area, make sure you give them a good wipe down first.



Charcoal and ash

If your grill isn’t electric then you are going to be left with some charcoal and ash after your summer barbecue.

And while many people assume this can be thrown away immediately after cooking, its better to wait.

“Charcoal can retain heat for much longer than people expect,” Ward warned.

And even if it appears cold on the surface, embers underneath can remain hot enough to start a fire several hours later.

Disposable grills

Similarly, your disposable barbecue also needs some time to cool off before you toss it in the bin.



“Disposable barbecues should never be placed in a wheelie bin while they’re still hot or warm,” Ward explained.

Councils and waste operators often deal with fires caused by barbecues that haven’t cooled down properly before being thrown away.

You should also check your local council guidance for disposing of these grills, as disposal rules can vary between areas.

Gas cannisters

Whether you’re using a camping stove or a barbecue, your gas canister will require special handling and cannot be recycled at home.

“Gas canisters should never be placed in general household waste or recycling bins,” the expert advised.



These items can become extremely dangerous if disposed of incorrectly.

Particularly if they are placed in a compacter during waste processing.

Plastic food containers

Finally, make sure you take the right steps when disposing of plastic food containers.

Many barbecue food products are wrapped in multiple layers of packaging, which means they can’t always be placed in the plastic recycling bin.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Not all plastics are recyclable, even if they look similar,” Ward said.



Make sure you don’t mix non-recyclable packaging into recycling bins as this can contaminate collections, creating additional processing costs.

News.title: ‘Grooming gang’ charged with rape and sexual abuse against eight children over ten-year period
News.content:
'RAPE' CHARGES ‘Grooming gang’ charged with rape and sexual abuse against eight children over ten-year period

EIGHT suspected grooming gang members have been charged with rape and sexual abuse against children over a decade-long period.

The men, aged 54 to 73, were arrested in areas across the UK following a major investigation into alleged offences between 1985 and 1996.

Some 34 charges – including 17 of rape – have been brought against the suspects following the probe into historical child sexual exploitation.

Operation Oak investigated sexual abuse claims made by eight women who were all children at the time of the alleged offences.





The men were arrested in Newport, Swansea, London, Birmingham, Lancashire, Edinburgh and the Argyll and Bute area of Scotland.

The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) has since authorised the charges, some of which relate to multiple incidents of rape.

Gwent Police confirmed the men are set to appear before Newport Magistrates’ Court on July 24.

Detective Chief Superintendent Andrew Tuck urged any victims of abuse to come forward and speak to police.

Men charged as part of Operation Oak Shafaq Mohammed, 58 Four counts of rape of a female under 16, three counts of rape of a female aged 16 years or over, two counts of aiding and abetting the rape of a female under 16, causing the prostitution of a girl under 16, causing the prostitution of a woman. Syed Mohammad Ashan Taqvi, 65 Three counts of rape of a female under 16. Mohammed Sheikh Abdul Hannan, 54 Two counts of rape of a female aged 16 years or over, one count of indecent assault on a woman over 16 years of age, three counts of aiding and abetting the rape of a female under 16 years of age or over and two counts of conspiring to rape a woman aged 16 years or over. Kevin Lawrence, 54 Two counts of conspiring to rape a woman aged 16 years or over and causing the prostitution of a woman. Sheikh Mohammed Tahir Ullah, 73 One count of rape of a female aged 16 years or over and one count of rape of a female under 16. Aminur Rahman Chowdhury, 58 One count of rape of a female aged 16 years or over. Shakeel Babur, 58 Four counts of indecent assault on a girl under the age of 16. Murad Ali, 57 Two counts of rape of a female under 16.

Mr Tuck said: “Operation Oak is a complex and long-running investigation into group-based child sexual exploitation in south Wales.

“At the heart of our investigation has been supporting victims. Together with specialist agencies, we are continuing to provide support to them.

“Anyone who reports child abuse will be taken seriously.

“We would urge anyone who has suffered abuse or has concerns about someone who may be suffering to come forward.



“We will listen to you and investigate all offences, and also ensure you have access to any help or support you need.”

Jenny Hopkins, chief crown prosecutor for Wales, said there was “sufficient evidence” to take the men to court.

She added: “Our prosecutors have worked to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring the case to court and that it is in the public interest to pursue criminal proceedings.

“We remind all concerned that criminal proceedings against these defendants are active and that they have the right to a fair trial.

“It is vital that there should be no reporting, commentary or sharing of information online which could in any way prejudice these proceedings.”

News.title: ‘Black Widow’ carer who kept OAP like ‘caged animal’ & stole £300k before fleeing to Tenerife is finally arrested
News.content:
A FRAUDSTER dubbed “the Black Widow” has finally been arrested – one year after she fled the country for her holiday home in Tenerife, The Sun understands.

It comes after The Sun tracked down fugitive Pamela Gwinnett as she sunbathed and relaxed in bars in her holiday island bolthole.



The twisted carer stole £300,000 from her “cash cow” Joan Greene and fled the country before she could be brought to justice.

She took up residence in her flat at a Brit tourist hotspot, with locals telling The Sun she spent her time sunbathing and drinking in bars.



The heartless 62-year-old, originally from Adlington, Cheshire, systematically plundered thousands from retired accountant Joan after setting herself up as the pensioner’s carer.

Gwinnett continued to steal money from Joan, 89, even after the pensioner passed away.

She was arrested for fraud by abuse of position and theft, but released on bail.

The carer applied for permission to fly to Tenerife, claiming she needed to scatter her brother’s ashes, which the court refused.

But five hours later, she was on a plane and fled the UK.

In her absence, the cruel monster was sentenced to six years in prison at Preston Crown Court – and the Judge Michael Maher called for help from the public and press to bring her back.



Greater Manchester Police have now confirmed cops have finally swooped on her flat and arrested the fraudster.

The Sun previously revealed the fugitive was hiding in plain sight, flaunting her freedom by sunbathing and going to bars in Tenerife.

Fuming locals told The Sun they recognised Gwinnett from her mugshot – and are glad she has finally been dragged out, but wonder why it took so long.



One told The Sun: “It’s a small place, everyone knows everyone, and she’s always out and about.

“She’s very well known there.”

She was living in a penthouse apartment in a sunny town on the south-west coast of Tenerife, according to locals. It has since been locked up and the outside furniture taken in.

It is understood she also owns another apartment, which The Sun found on various holiday let websites priced at £112 a night – and it is booked solid until April.

The lavish seaside property has access to a pool, “stunning views”, a balcony, a big TV and a more than 8 out of 10 rating on a booking website.



But guests were seemingly cottoning on to who their host is – with some reviews naming “Pam” and one saying she is wanted by UK police.

The host responded by saying the post was “slander” – and said “get your facts right”.

One British pensioner told The Sun he met her in a bar, saying she tried to rent him a plush flat.



But later he discovered her “devious, evil crimes”.

The 66-year-old from Leeds said: “She’s certainly not hiding. I see her swanning about town, sometimes with some bloke – definitely British. It’s disgusting.

“She’s living off ill-gotten gains after robbing that sweet old lady of her dignity and her family.

“Spanish police need to pick her up. How is she allowed to just sunbathe all day? It’s abhorrent.”

Another raging pensioner told The Sun how Gwinnett appears “very pleasant and quite attractive” on the island.



She said Gwinnett has been visiting the area for a number of years, but moved there full-time in April.

“It’s terrible that she’s done that to that elderly lady who has since died, and she’s just pottering about freely.”

Others fumed that the wicked 62-year-old is “knocking around bars” looking “very glamorous” and “dolled up”.



Neighbours say they contacted the police demanding to know when Gwinnett would be hauled back to face justice.

Judge Maher issued a confiscation order, ordering the sale of Gwinnett’s house in the UK to repay Joan’s family.

The Black Widow owns a £200,000 redbrick house on a sleepy residential street in the leafy village of Adlington, Chorley, in Lancashire.

Those in the quiet northern town told The Sun they never expected her to be capable of such horrible acts.

Gwinnett seemingly hid her evil intentions behind a friendly façade, all the while keeping the vulnerable OAP caged like an animal at her home in Chorley.



Residents well remember her “midnight flit” as she fled the country last year.

Another neighbour, hopeful that the Black Widow would be caught and prosecuted, told us that Gwinnett “deserves what’s coming.”

“We didn’t know anything was happening until it all came out – it was quite shocking, you wouldn’t have expected it from Pam,” they said.

In the past, she rented out her home in the UK. An ex-tenant told The Sun: “She was a nasty horrible lady, she left us with no heating or hot water all over Christmas.

“The house was had exposed wires and she refused to get them fixed.”



Gwinnett’s barrister Abigail Holmes previously said her client intends to appeal the convictions for fraud and theft.

The carer had claimed she was the grandmother’s carer but isolated frail, vulnerable Joan from her family.

She accused family members of mistreating the widow and did everything she could to keep them away while she fleeced her “golden goose.”

The carer spent money she stole from the “frail” 89-year-old on an Audi Q2, expensive meals, designer clothes, mortgages and Botox.

By the time Gwinnett’s power of attorney over Joan was suspended, she had already stolen £161,000 from the pensioner – and continued to do so after her death.



A court heard that the last months of Joan’s life had become “pock marked with increasing periods of bewilderment and confusion.”

The gran became doubly incontinent, but instead of looking after the elderly woman Gwinnett “bullied” her, the court was told.

In a heartbreaking video, Joan’s family are heard trying to comfort her while confronting Gwinnett.

Joan can be heard asking what is going on in the background, as grandson David reassures her: “People are looking out for you nan, people are looking out for you. We have your best interests at heart.”

Heartlessly, Gwinnett removes his hand from Joan’s and tells her: “Look at those lying eyes Joan.”



David is heard saying: “This is wrong. There’s only one person who is in the wrong. Give us a love nan. Love you. It’s alright.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Joan’s step-daughter Katherine Farrimond, 65, said Joan believed in her final years that her family “hated her” and “didn’t want to see her” because of Gwinnett’s “lies”.

David told The Sun: “We were all disgusted – she’d used nan like a piggy bank.”

News.title: Joe Biden gives first health update in months after cancer diagnosis as he announces new book about presidency
News.content:
FORMER President Joe Biden has revealed his cancer treatment is “going really well” in a rare personal health update as he announced a new book about his four years in the White House.

The 83-year-old thanked supporters for their prayers and well-wishes as he spoke about spending more time with his family while battling the disease.



In a video released on Wednesday, Biden said, “I’ve been spending a lot of time with my family. I’m dealing with a cancer diagnosis, been getting treatment, and it’s going really well.”

“I want to thank all those who have offered their prayers and support and well-wishes. It’s meant the world to me and to Jill.”



The update came as publishers Little Brown and Company announced that Biden’s presidential memoir, Promise Me, America, will be released on November 17.

The book will look back at the major crises and decisions that defined his one term in the White House, including the controversial end of hid 2024 re-election campaign.

READ MORE ON NEWS SENIOR MOMENT Joe Biden wanders around stage & shouts for granddaughter in troubling clip

“‘Promise Me, America’ is about the challenges we faced as a nation. It’s about the decisions I made and why I made them,” Biden said.

“Most of all, it’s about my faith in the promise of America.”

Biden said the memoir will explore leading the country through the Covid pandemic, rebuilding the economy and the aftermath of the January 6 attack on the US Capitol.



It will also cover the withdrawal from Afghanistan, his efforts to strengthen NATO and US support for Ukraine.

The former president said he will address why he initially chose to seek a second term, and why he later made the dramatic decision to step aside.

Biden dropped out of the 2024 presidential race in July that year following mounting concerns about his age and fitness for office.

Then-Vice President Kamala Harris replaced him as the Democratic nominee before losing the election to Donald Trump.

Biden was diagnosed with prostate cancer in May 2025 after experiencing urinary symptoms and doctors discovered a nodule.



His office said at the time that the aggressive cancer had spread to his bones and had a Gleason score of 9.

However, doctors found the cancer was hormone-sensitive, meaning it could respond to treatment.

Biden later underwent radiation therapy and hormone treatment, with his team announcing in October 2025 that he had complete a round of radiation.

His latest remarks did not offer further medical details but just a note about how his treatment has been progressing.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

A Little, Brown spokesperson told the Associated Press that Biden also plans to tour in support of the memoir and give interviews.



The publisher has not disclosed the financial terms of the book deal.

News.title: Depraved deacon preyed on homeless men & abused them while Church turned a blind eye – as fears grow over MORE victims
News.content:
CHURCH deacon John Grant smiled benevolently as he dished out soup to the homeless.

As a prominent member of the Baptist Church, nobody blinked an eyelid when he offered men a temporary place to live in his £500,000 home in leafy Muswell Hill, London.



But behind the scenes, wolfish Grant had already been grooming and abusing vulnerable young men for years – and The Sun can today reveal that the church KNEW he was a sex offender.

Grant, 77, who also ran youth clubs, even told church bosses he had a problem – but they suggested he get counselling instead of going to the cops.



Now police fear he could have victims all over the UK after his abuse went on for more than four decades.

The detective who finally brought him to justice said: “This was textbook grooming.



“His church work facilitated his offending.”

Grant’s twisted crimes only came to light when one of his victims complained to a minister at a totally different Anglican church, who got in touch with the baptist safeguarding officers.



The first complaint about Grant came in the 70s when he was a leader at Billingham Baptist Church in Stockton-on-Tees. His victim told church seniors he had been assaulted but they dealt with it internally, giving Grant a slap on the wrist.

In 1984, he moved to Muswell Hill Baptist Church and six years later he told deacons that he had inappropriately touched a young man.

He only admitted it after his victim threatened to tell church leaders and, even then, downplayed it, claiming he touched him ‘too far up his leg’.

Astonishingly, they suggested he get counselling but it’s not known if any help was offered to his victim.

Justice finally caught up with Grant this week when he was found guilty of three counts of sexual assault, six of indecent of indecent assault and two counts of causing a victim to engage in non-penetrative sexual activity.



He will be sentenced in September for the offences which related to four victims aged between 18 and 25, from 1970 to 2012.

One of his victims had already died but police managed to secure a conviction on evidence given by others, including his wife.

Police have now appealed for more potential victims to come forward from both Billingham and Muswell Hill as well as Broomsknoll Church of Scotland in Airdrie, which Grant attended between 1965 and 1970, and Ward Green Baptist Church in Barnsley, where he went between 1973 and 1984.

His most senior role was at Muswell where he was a moderator for the London Baptist Association, which saw him preach at other churches around the area.

Detective constable Liam Levy, who led the investigation, which he described as “a distressing case” said one of Grant’s victims was previously involved in an altercation with the deacon.



He said: “The earliest complaint about Grant relates to his time at Billingham when, sometime during the 1970s, a complaint was made against him but it was dealt with internally.

“In 1990, he self-reported to the deacons at Muswell Hill that there had been an incident between him and a young man and, again, it was dealt with as a conversation. There was mention of him needing counselling.

“Two of his victims were very vulnerable after he met them through his work at a soup kitchen, one was homeless and the other was about to be made homeless.

“He took them both into his homes at different times.”



The first complaint to police came in 2023 and DC Levy managed to track down other victims, including one who had a physical altercation with the ex-deacon in 2008.

DC Levy said: “We don’t know how many other victims there might be, but there’s a strong belief that there are more out there.

“It’s a concern for me that, due to Grant’s age, there could be other complainants that have since passed away but we have demonstrated that we can press charges and secure a conviction.

“In interview, Grant was quite subdued. He would pick and choose when to be open. He would freely talk about the work he’d done in the church and was happy to tell us where he’d been in the past, but when it came down to the core of the offending he would shut down and revert to ‘no comment’.

“I got the impression that his work was a point of pride for him, something he relied upon and referred to throughout his life.



“Unfortunately it facilitated his offending and gave him an open door to vulnerable people.

“Some of his victims put on a brave face but it undoubtedly changed their lives completely.”

Reverend Mike Lowe, of the Baptist Union of Great Britain, which oversees churches, said safeguarding has changed “massively” over the time of Grant’s offending.

The Union said it was “shocked and saddened” and was “committed towards excellence in safeguarding.”

A statement from the London Baptist Association said it “deeply condemned” Grant’s actions.



It added: “We recognise the immense courage it takes for victim-survivors to come forward, particularly when offences occurred many years ago and involve someone who held positions of trust and influence within our churches.

“Mr Grant was a prominent and influential figure in the life of the London Baptist Association for many years.

“He served in a number of voluntary leadership roles, including as a Trustee and Moderator of our charity, and preached widely across our family of churches.

“This case is a sobering reminder that positions of authority within our churches can be misused.

“It reinforces the importance of robust safeguarding, healthy accountability, and ensuring that our churches are places where people are safe, where concerns are heard, and where action is taken.



“Our Regional Safeguarding Lead supported the initial report to police, maintained contact throughout the investigation, and provided a formal witness statement. Throughout, our priority has been to support victim-survivors, cooperate fully with the police investigation, and help the church respond with care, integrity, and transparency.”

The Church refused to be drawn on specific details of previous allegations dealt with by leadership.

News.title: King’s Guard forced to sound emergency alarm as horse almost collapses in scorching heat
News.content:
King’s Guard forced to sound emergency alarm as horse almost collapses in scorching heat

A horse in the King’s Guard has almost passed out in sweltering London temperatures, forcing the officer to pull an alarm as concerned tourists watched the incident unfold at Whitehall

View 3 Images Tourists were concerned when the horse started stumbling in the heat (Image: Mirrorpix)

A member of the King’s Guard was forced to sound an emergency alarm after his horse almost collapsed in the scorching heat.

‌



The stoic officer appeared concerned for the animal he sat atop, as the horse continuously dropped his head and stumbled on Monday. Concerned tourists watched on as the Guard firmly pressed an emergency alarm, as London was hit with sweltering 30 degree heat.

‌



The footage captured by an onlooker shows the guardsman, dressed in a bright scarlet wool tunic and dark trousers, and his horse briefly waiting for another service member to relieve the animal from its station at Whitehall.

‌

Content cannot be displayed without consent

Then, after a tourist quickly takes an opportunity to take a picture with the horse, a soldier emerges from behind the gates to help. After the guard tends to the alarm, the soldier leads the horse and rider from their post outside of the Household Cavalry Museum to the safety of the shade.

The horse's legs appeared to be unsteady in the heat as it vanished behind the gates. The footage, which has been viewed over 200,000 times, left many viewers shocked, with one writing: “This shouldn't be happening.”

‌



Another said: “Traditional or not, common sense prevails - it's too flipping hot for both horse and human.” The moment comes just weeks after another of the King’s Guard horses became erratic in the late May heatwave, which saw the UK reach the hottest temperatures ever recorded at the time.

View 3 Images The King's Guards on horseback (Image: Dinendra Haria/SOPA Images/Shutterstock)

On the May bank holiday weekend, tourists scrambled out of the way as a horse became agitated in the blazing heat. Footage captured the moment the animal suddenly began circling outside Horse Guards Parade in central London, tossing its head and stamping around in front of stunned crowds.

‌



In a rare break from strict protocol, another guard was seen emerging from the Horse Guards Building to calm the horse down, gently stroking it and attempting to settle it before it was eventually led away from the heat. In late June, continually rising temperatures impacted the traditional Changing of the Guard ceremonies at Buckingham Palace and Windsor Castle, which were cancelled for several days.

View 3 Images The Changing of the Guard was cancelled due to the hot weather (Image: Geoffrey Swaine/Shutterstock)

‌



The ceremonies, which take place most days outside the royal residences, see visitors gather to see soldiers in their heavy bearskin hats and red tunic process to and from buildings to the sound of a military band, with horses taking part. The Army In London, which puts on the ceremonies, said they had to be cancelled in order to protect soldiers, horses and spectators, who watch the spectacle.

It explained in a statement: “The well-being of our soldiers, military working horses, and the public who gather in large numbers to watch these events is always our priority. We know this is a busy and popular time of year to visit, and we're sorry if this is disappointing. Thank you for your understanding, and please do follow the Met Office advice to stay safe in the heat.”

The Household Troops - or Guards - have protected the Sovereign since 1660 and have been patrolling outside Buckingham Palace since Queen Victoria made it her official residence in 1837.

News.title: Mum who murdered son, 5, attends his inquest from prison and wants her sentence cut
News.content:
Mum who murdered son, 5, attends his inquest from prison and wants her sentence cut

Angharad Williamson, 34, watched the pre-inquest into her five-year-old son Logan Mwangi's death from prison, where she is serving at least 28 years for his murder

View 5 Images Logan Mwangi was murdered at just five-years-old (Image: PA)

A mum who murdered her five-year-old son before his body was found dumped in a river has attended a pre-inquest into the child's death.

‌



Angharad Williamson, 34, watched the hearing online from HMP Downview in Surrey, where she is serving at least 28 years for the murder of Logan Mwangi.

‌



The youngster was found with 56 external injuries, as well as a torn liver and trauma to the brain following a horrific campaign of abuse at his family home in Bridgend, South Wales.

‌



Despite being under the care of social services, none of Logan's injuries prior to his death - a broken arm, broken collarbone and burns to his skin - raised alarm bells with authorities.

View 5 Images Angharad Williamson was jailed for the murder of Logan (Image: PA)

Williamson's then partner John Cole, 41, and stepson Craig Mulligan, 14, were also convicted of the murder of Logan after his death in July 2021.

‌



Cole dumped Logan's dead body in the River Ogmore - a spot where he would regularly fly-tip rubbish just 400 yards from the family home, reports Wales Online.

A pre-inquest review into Logan's death began today at Pontypridd Coroner's Court before coroner David Regan.

Representatives from local health chiefs, social services and South Wales Police all attended the largely administrative hearing which was held both in court and via Teams.

‌



View 5 Images The hearing took place at Pontypridd Coroner's Court (Image: MEDIA WALES)

Williamson had denied Logan's murder and claimed she was asleep when his body was dumped at the river. But evidence found she had been using her phone throughout the night and turning lights on and off in the house when nobody else was home.

Williamson tried to have her conviction overturned via the Court of Appeal but her bid was rejected in January 2023.

‌



The court heard she has since requested a former senior police officer to attend the hearing as a lay person to carry out a review of her conviction to see if she can further appeal to the criminal cases review board.

The former officer, Tony Thompson, said he was working "pro-bono" to carry out an investigation and would attend the hearing.

View 5 Images John Cole, 41, dumped Logan's body in the River Ogmore (Image: PA)

‌



Horrific details of Logan's abuse were laid bare during a nine week trial in 2022.

The court was told how Logan had tested positive for Covid-19 and was treated like a prisoner in the days leading up to his death, with the five-year-old confined to his tiny bedroom behind a locked child gate.

He was repeatedly punished by Williamson and Cole when he tried to leave the room and interact with his family, the court heard. This was also despite their knowledge that Logan would self-harm by biting himself until he bled.

‌



Prosecutor Caroline Rees KC told the trial: "He had been kept like a prisoner in his small bedroom - a room described by Angharad Williamson as 'like a dungeon' with the curtains closed and a barred child's gate stopping him from moving about the rest of the flat.

"That little boy was being made to face a wall as food was being delivered so other members of the house did not catch Covid. What must have he thought of the way his life was in these 10 days?

"He was dehumanised by each of the defendants."

‌



View 5 Images Williamson's stepson Craig Mulligan (Image: PA)

Logan had been on the child protection register for seven months before his death - but following a review, he was stepped down from being a "child in protection" to a "child in need" just weeks before he was killed.

Ms Rees said Angharad Williamson was "a liar" who "tried to portray herself as a loving mother who was over-protective to Logan's interests - this was, as so much is about Angharad Williamson in the context of this case, a total sham".

‌



"She has been exposed as a selfish woman whose only protective interest was to herself," she added. "Even by her own words she accepts she was a 's*** mother' to Logan - a rare moment of truth during her time in the witness box."

Medical experts said Logan's injuries were such that they were compared to a "fall from a great height" or a "high velocity road traffic collision".

Williamson, Cole and Mulligan were all jailed for life. Williamson was given a minimum term of 28 years.

Article continues below

A further hearing into Logan's death is scheduled for November.

News.title: Man arrested 'for threatening to shoot Nigel Farage'
News.content:
Man arrested 'for threatening to shoot Nigel Farage'

The Met Police have confirmed a man is under arrest for allegedly threatening Reform UK leader Nigel Farage and has now been released on bail

View 2 Images Reform UK leader Nigel Farage is helping police (Image: Jordan Pettitt/PA Wire)

A man has been arrested for allegedly threatening Nigel Farage, the Met Police have confirmed.

An individual was only arrested yesterday on suspicion of sending a threatening communication. He was questioned before being released on bail as the police investigations continue.

It is claimed the arrest was prompted by parliamentary authorities, who ordered police to investigate a threat to the Reform UK leader.

"On Tuesday, 14 July a man in his 20s was arrested by Met officers on suspicion of sending threatening communications to a Member of Parliament," the Met Police told the Mirror.

View 2 Images Farage lays flowers outside the home of Anne Widdecombe (Image: Wayne Perry)

“The arrest relates to a social media post from earlier this year, which was reported to police on Friday, 8 May. After receiving the report, detectives submitted an application to a social media platform to gain access to the user’s contact information.

“After the relevant information was returned to detectives the man was arrested, with support from local Met officers, at a residential address in south London. After being held in police custody overnight, he has since been bailed pending further enquiries.”

The arrest comes after the murder of Ann Widdecombe, which Devon and Cornwall Police have described as a targeted attack. Detectives have obtained a warrant under the Terrorism Act to hold a 28-year-old male suspect arrested in Rotherham, Yorkshire, on suspicion of murder.

Now, The Telegraph reports that a man told Mr Farage: “I am going to shoot you in the head if you win."

Earlier today, Reform Home Affairs spokesman Zia Yusuf said all MPs past and present will be given around-the-clock security should the party win the next general election.

“Enough is enough,” he said at a press conference this morning. “I do not want to see another politician killed like our dear Ann. This has to stop.

“I will close by announcing a new Reform policy. If Reform win the next general election, I will ensure all members of parliament -from all parties - are provided with around-the-clock protection.

“We will allocate significant new resources to protect former politicians still active in public life.”

The body of Miss Widdecombe, 78, was discovered on Thursday 9 July at her home in Devon. She had sustained serious injuries in an attack police state took place the previous day.

On Monday, a white British man, 28, was arrested before being re-arrested on Monday on suspicion of the commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism.

Keir Starmers Greatest Hits

Keir Starmer will depart as PM next week after six years in charge of the Labour party.

In his final Cabinet meeting on Wednesday morning, Mr Starmer highlighted his proudest achievements while in government, pointing to the UK economy, improvements to the NHS and investment in tackling child poverty.

He told ministers his administration had “transformed our international standing” as he hailed his efforts to reset ties with the European Union and take a leading role in the coalition of the willing on Ukraine and a future mission to secure the Strait of Hormuz.

It comes as MPs from all parties paid tribute to the outgoing-PM, who pledged to give his “wholehearted support” to Andy Burnham "privately if asked for, not publicly when not asked for”.

News.title: Cosmetic surgery warning update following rare cases of medical condition
News.content:
Cosmetic surgery warning update following rare cases of medical condition

The MHRA is strengthening safety warnings for all the products

View 2 Images Rare cases of botulism linked to their use (stock image) (Image: Getty)

In a new update issued today (July 15), the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) confirmed it is stepping up its safety warnings for all products containing botulinum toxin type A due to rare reports of botulism linked to these products. While this toxin is commonly used in both medical and cosmetic procedures, it can sometimes spread beyond the intended area.

‌



This spread can lead to botulism, which is a serious and potentially fatal illness. Botulinum toxin type A is a prescription-only medicine (POM) in the UK. It is authorised to treat a number of conditions, including muscle spasms, hyperhidrosis (excess sweating from armpits), and an overactive bladder.

‌



To raise more awareness about iatrogenic botulism—botulism that occurs due to medical treatment—the MHRA has worked with manufacturers to improve product labels and patient information leaflets. Botulism is a rare but life-threatening condition that attacks the nervous system.

‌



Common symptoms include muscle weakness, breathing difficulties, slurred speech, or difficulty swallowing. If patients experience these symptoms within four weeks after treatment, they are strongly encouraged to seek immediate medical attention.

Dr Alison Cave, MHRA Chief Safety Officer, said: " Botulinum toxin products are effective for a number of different medical and cosmetic purposes when used correctly. However, these strengthened warnings are an important reminder that, in rare cases, serious side effects can occur.

Content cannot be displayed without consent

‌



“It is vital that healthcare professionals and patients are aware of the symptoms of botulism and act quickly if they arise as this is a medical emergency. We also strongly urge the public to avoid unlicensed products and seek treatment only from appropriately qualified practitioners. The MHRA continuously monitors the safety of these medicines, including side effects and emerging evidence."

Dr Martin Bewley, Consultant in Health Protection from UKHSA, said: " While botulism is a rare infection, it can be serious. There are effective treatments available and we recommend seeking immediate medical advice if you have had a recent treatment and are having symptoms such as difficulty swallowing.

"Contact NHS 111 (or local equivalent in Northern Ireland) for further advice and seek immediate medical attention. It is important to get checked out so you can have peace of mind and treatment if needed. Given the risks, it is also important to go to a licensed practitioner."

‌



View 2 Images Patients who experience the symptoms are urged to seek immediate medical attention (stock image)

If you're planning to get botulinum toxin for a cosmetic treatment, the NHS provides helpful information to help you select a suitable prescriber. The risk of adverse reactions may be higher in certain circumstances, including;

in patients with certain underlying conditions, such as neurological disorders, a history of dysphagia (difficult swallowing) or a history of aspiration (breathing in a foreign material)

where high doses are used

where products are used outside of their licensed indications or into an unapproved site.

Article continues below

The MHRA is highlighting significant risks associated with unlicensed and counterfeit botulinum toxin products, which fail to meet UK safety and quality standards.
